title: Cage-related crystal-field effects in the paramagnetic range of PrB$_6$
authors: Mehdi Amara, Christine Opagiste, Natalya Yu. Shitsevalova
abstract: New insights into the paramagnetic range of PrB$_6$ below 50 K are revealed through specific-heat, thermal-expansion and magnetic measurements. The latent heats of the two successive magnetic transitions, together with an improved description of the lattice contribution, enable a detailed determination of the thermal variation of the magnetic entropy. Immediately above the first-order magnetic ordering temperature ($T_N = 6.7$ K), the magnetic entropy per Pr$^{3+}$ is close to that of a doublet, instead of the triplet crystal-field ground state identified by inelastic neutron scattering. Temperatures in excess of 30 K are required to reach the entropy of the threefold-degenerate ground state. This is reminiscent of the CeB$_6$ case and, similarly, strongly suggests a dynamical splitting of the crystal-field ground state within the boron cage. Further evidence of this splitting is provided by the analysis of the low-temperature paramagnetic susceptibility, which resembles that of a non-magnetic ground state. In addition, a large thermal-expansion anomaly is observed below 20 K, consistent with the expected centrifugal Jahn-Teller effect.
summary: This work uses detailed measurements of specific heat, thermal expansion, and magnetization on PrB6 to probe its magnetic behavior in the paramagnetic regime. The key finding suggests that the crystal-field ground state undergoes a dynamical splitting, evidenced by the measured magnetic entropy matching a doublet state rather than the expected triplet state. This points toward complex electronic interactions within the boron cage structure.
main_problem: The study aims to gain new insights into the paramagnetic range of PrB6 below 50 K, specifically investigating cage-related crystal-field effects.
main_result: The magnetic entropy immediately above the first-order magnetic ordering temperature is close to that of a doublet, suggesting a dynamical splitting of the crystal-field ground state within the boron cage.
method: The research combines specific-heat, thermal-expansion, and magnetic susceptibility measurements to analyze the thermal variation of the magnetic entropy.
model_or_system: The physical system is the rare-earth hexaboride compound PrB6. The analysis compares experimental data against theoretical models describing crystal-field splitting and lattice contributions.
key_observables: Magnetic entropy per Pr3+, latent heats of magnetic transitions (T_N=6.7 K, T*=3.9 K), low-temperature paramagnetic susceptibility, and thermal expansion anomalies.
important_parameters: Temperatures below 50 K, the magnetic ordering temperatures (T_N, T*), and the comparison between doublet/triplet ground state entropies.
main_assumptions: The analysis requires an improved description of the lattice contribution to the specific heat, and the interpretation relies on analogies with CeB6.
figures_summary: Figures show specific heat data, latent heat calculations at magnetic transitions, and thermal expansion comparisons between PrB6 and non-magnetic references.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first measuring thermodynamic quantities (specific heat, thermal expansion) to determine magnetic entropy changes across magnetic transitions, then analyzing the low-temperature susceptibility and thermal expansion anomalies to deduce the nature of the crystal-field ground state splitting.
why_interesting: The investigation into how crystal-field effects manifest in the thermal properties and magnetic entropy of a solid-state material provides insights into strong electronic correlations and orbital degrees of freedom.
